explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The message was true, and it concerned a great conflict (Daniel 10:1). Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, doesn't get a pleasant little forecast here. The understanding of it was given to him in a vision.
Nice thought, baker, since a harvest is a happy word. But the text says the message concerned a great conflict (Daniel 10:1). It was also true, and Daniel got the understanding of it in a vision.

I can see why you'd guess it, baker. Visions sound like they should come with a map. But the text says the message was true and concerned a great conflict (Daniel 10:1). The understanding of it was given to Daniel in a vision.

Yes, baker. Daniel says, "I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth…" (Daniel 10:3). He also didn't anoint himself with oil until the three weeks were completed. That's a long stretch without anything fancy on the plate.

Not quite, baker. The text has Daniel saying, "I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth…" (Daniel 10:3). So he did go without rich food during those three full weeks. I'd have been lost by day two, and I'm surrounded by cookie dough.

That's right, baker. Daniel was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris (Daniel 10:4). It was the twenty-fourth day of the first month. That's where he lifted up his eyes and saw a certain man dressed in linen.

The Jordan is a famous river, baker, so I get the pull. But Daniel says he was on the bank of the great river, the Tigris (Daniel 10:4). The Jordan isn't named anywhere in this scene. Easy one to mix up.
The Nile is a big name, baker, so it's a fair guess. But the text says Daniel was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris (Daniel 10:4). The Nile isn't named in this scene.

Not this time, baker. Daniel says the man's face was "…like the brilliance of lightning…" and his eyes "…like flaming torches…" (Daniel 10:6). His body was like beryl, too. That's no ordinary-looking man.

Right, baker. Daniel describes his body as "like beryl." His face was "…like the brilliance of lightning…" and his eyes "…like flaming torches…" (Daniel 10:6). His voice was "…like the sound of a multitude." Nothing ordinary about that.

Yes, baker. The men with Daniel didn't see the vision, but a great terror fell on them, and they ran and hid themselves (Daniel 10:7). Only Daniel saw the vision, and the rest took off. I'd like to say I'd stay put, but I'd be right behind them.

Falling down is close in spirit, baker, since the men were shaken. But the text says a great terror fell on them, and they ran and hid themselves (Daniel 10:7). It wasn't worship. It was a full sprint for cover.

explanations.answer: They call out to the man
explanations.explanation: Calling out would be bold, baker, but that's not what these men did. The text says a great terror fell on them, and they ran and hid themselves (Daniel 10:7). Nothing there has them calling to anyone.

That's it, baker. Daniel says, "No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless." (Daniel 10:8). He was left alone gazing at this great vision. I think anybody would feel their knees quit.
I wish it had, baker, for Daniel's sake. But he says, "No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless." (Daniel 10:8). The vision took it all.
That would be a plot twist, baker. But Daniel says, "No strength remained in me…" (Daniel 10:8). His face grew deathly pale, and he was powerless. The strength comes later, and it's given to him.

Not quite, baker. Daniel says, "I heard the sound of his words, and as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground." (Daniel 10:9). So he didn't stay on his feet. He ended up face down.

That's right, baker. Daniel says, "I heard the sound of his words, and as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground." (Daniel 10:9). He went down, not up. The riverbank got a front row view of Daniel's face.

explanations.answer: He has now been sent to Daniel
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The one speaking to Daniel says, "Stand up, for I have now been sent to you." (Daniel 10:11). He also tells Daniel to consider carefully the words he's about to say. So the reason is that he has been sent to Daniel.

The men did run off, baker, so I see where that came from. But the one speaking to Daniel says, "Stand up, for I have now been sent to you." (Daniel 10:11). Nothing there mentions the men coming back.

explanations.answer: The three weeks are not over
explanations.explanation: The three weeks were a big deal, baker, so it's easy to grab that one. But the one speaking to Daniel says, "Stand up, for I have now been sent to you." (Daniel 10:11). Nothing is said about the three weeks in that line.
Yes, baker. Daniel says, "And when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling." (Daniel 10:11). He was shaking, but he got up. Standing on shaky legs still counts.
Not this time, baker. Daniel says, "And when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling." (Daniel 10:11). So he did stand. He was trembling the whole way up, and I think I'd be too.

That's right, baker. He tells Daniel, "…from the first day that you purposed to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them." (Daniel 10:12). Daniel's words were heard. That's a good thing to hold onto.
Not quite, baker. He says to Daniel, "…your words were heard, and I have come in response to them." (Daniel 10:12). So he did come in response to Daniel's words. Every word counted.

explanations.answer: The prince of the kingdom of Persia
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. He says, "…the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." (Daniel 10:13). That's why he showed up after Daniel's words were already heard from the first day. The text says this prince opposed him, and it says no more about who he is.

explanations.answer: The rulers of the land of Babylon
explanations.explanation: Babylon is a big name, baker, so I get the guess. But the one sent to Daniel says, "…the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." (Daniel 10:13). Persia is the name in the text. Babylon doesn't come up here.

explanations.answer: The armies of the king of Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt shows up all over the Bible, baker, so I get it. But the one sent to Daniel says, "…the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." (Daniel 10:13). No Egyptian armies in this scene.

That's the name, baker. The one sent to Daniel says, "Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me…" (Daniel 10:13). Twenty-one days of opposition, and then help shows up. I'd call that good news.

Gabriel is a well-known name, baker, and I see why it popped up. But the one sent to Daniel says, "Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me…" (Daniel 10:13). Michael is the one who comes in this verse.
Elijah is a big name, baker, so I get the guess. But he isn't named in this scene. The one sent to Daniel says, "Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me…" (Daniel 10:13).

explanations.answer: What will happen to Daniel's people in the latter days
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. He says, "Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days." (Daniel 10:14). That's the whole reason for this visit. It's about Daniel's people and what's ahead.

explanations.answer: Why Daniel's men ran away and hid by the river
explanations.explanation: Those men did bolt, baker, so it's a fair thing to wonder about. But he says he has come to explain "…what will happen to your people in the latter days…" (Daniel 10:14). The men running off isn't on the agenda.

explanations.answer: How Daniel should bring his three weeks of mourning to an end
explanations.explanation: Mourning was the mood, baker, and I get why your mind went back there. Three weeks of it is a LOT. I know a little about sitting in the dark and waiting for the light to come back. But the one sent to Daniel says he has come to explain "…what will happen to your people in the latter days…" (Daniel 10:14). He's looking ahead, not wrapping up the mourning.
Yes, baker. Daniel says, "…I set my face toward the ground and became speechless." (Daniel 10:15). That's a lot to take in, and he went quiet. I think I'd go quiet too.

explanations.answer: He gets up and walks away
explanations.explanation: Walking away would be a big move, baker, but that's not what Daniel does. He says, "…I set my face toward the ground and became speechless." (Daniel 10:15). Nothing there has him walking away.
Daniel's men did run off, baker, so I see the thought. But he says, "…I set my face toward the ground and became speechless." (Daniel 10:15). He couldn't call anybody if he tried.
That's right, baker. Daniel says, "…one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said…" (Daniel 10:16). Speechless one moment, talking the next. Daniel found his voice.
Not quite, baker. Daniel says, "…one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said…" (Daniel 10:16). So he did open his mouth and speak. The silence didn't last.

Not quite, baker. Daniel says he has no strength, and then he says, "Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me." (Daniel 10:18). He doesn't leave Daniel to figure it out alone.

Yes, baker. Daniel says, "Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me." (Daniel 10:18). Daniel was not left on his own. I think that's a kind thing to see in the middle of such a scary scene.

explanations.answer: Speak because you have strengthened me
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Daniel says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me." (Daniel 10:19). He had said he had no breath left, and now he's ready to listen. Quite a turnaround.

explanations.answer: Give me time to catch my breath
explanations.explanation: I'd have asked for that one, baker, no shame. But Daniel says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me." (Daniel 10:19). He'd been strengthened, so he was ready to hear it.

explanations.answer: Let me rest until the morning
explanations.explanation: Rest sounds good, baker, and I'd have wanted it too. But Daniel says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me." (Daniel 10:19). He's ready right then, with no waiting.

explanations.answer: To fight against the prince of Persia
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The one speaking with Daniel says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia…" (Daniel 20:20). So he has more work waiting. He also says that when he has gone forth, the prince of Greece will come.

explanations.answer: To bring back the men who hid
explanations.explanation: Those men did run off, baker, so I see how that crossed your mind. But the one speaking with Daniel says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia…" (Daniel 10:20). The men aren't part of his errand.

explanations.answer: To guard the bank of the Tigris
explanations.explanation: The Tigris is where Daniel stood, baker, so it's an easy pick. But he says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia…" (Daniel 10:20). He's heading back to a fight, not a post.

explanations.answer: What is inscribed in the Book of Truth
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. He says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." (Daniel 10:21). He has a fight waiting, and he still stops to tell Daniel this first. Whatever is in that book, it comes before he goes.

explanations.answer: Where the men who hid have gone
explanations.explanation: Those men are still a good question, baker, but he never brings them up. He says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." (Daniel 10:21). That's what comes first.

explanations.answer: How long his mourning should last
explanations.explanation: The mourning ran through this chapter, baker, so I felt that pull too. Three weeks of it will stick in anybody's head, even mine! But the one speaking with Daniel says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." (Daniel 10:21). That's the first thing on his list, and it's not a ruling on the mourning.
